Hi Kimberly,

Thanks again for the product walkthrough yesterday. Aperture is ready to move forward with a limited pilot in APAC (Singapore region) that will run from July through September. Our SRE asked me to share the rough traffic profile so we can align on a dedicated pool proposal. High level:~

- Pilot scope: 3 customer-facing microservices (chat + summarization + embeddings lookup) behind our edge gateway
- Peak concurrency: ~180 concurrent user sessions across services (expected traffic spikes during morning and evening local time)
- Inference profile: ~6k tokens/session average; ~40 requests/sec sustained, occasional spikes to 120 req/sec for short windows
- Latency target: P95 <= 250ms for chat generate flows
- Start date target: 2027-07-15 (soft)

We want a hybrid approach: dedicated pool for sustained throughput with burst into hosted capacity if needed. Could you confirm what an APAC edge hybrid pool would look like (recommended GPU type, node counts, expected warmup times, and cost estimate for a 3-month pilot)? Also, our procurement requires an estimated monthly committed capacity and a point-of-contact for SOC2 evidence.

Attaching our pilot MVP statement for context.

Best,
Sophia Li
Head of Product, Aperture Health

Hi Sophia — thanks for the details and the MVP doc. Looping in Rishi (capacity planning) and Mina (onboarding/region ops) so we can push a concrete proposal. Initial thoughts inline below and a sizing workbook attached.

Quick answers up front:
- Recommended GPU: H100 80GB (sustained throughput for long-context chat + embeddings). If cost is a bigger constraint, we can propose an A100 80GB fallback with quantization recommendations.
- Baseline pool for pilot: 8x H100 nodes (estimate ~160 concurrent generation slots assuming optimized batching and prefix caching across services); add 4x burst-enabled nodes in hosted pool for spikes.
- Expected warmup: cold-start for newly loaded model variants ~60–90s for full KV cache; steady-state warm under 10–20s.
- SOC2 / evidence: we can provide the SOC2-type-2 report and our infra audit logs; Mina will send the long-form checklist.

Open questions we need answered to firm up numbers:
1) Token distribution per request (you gave average; do you have 90th percentile tokens?)
2) % of requests that are chat generate vs embeddings (embeddings are cheaper but throughput-limited differently)
3) Acceptable fallbacks for P95 latency if burst pool is saturated

I attached a first-pass sizing worksheet with two scenarios (H100 baseline and A100 fallback) and a short cost delta by month for the three-month pilot. Please review and flag the cells you want adjusted.

Next steps: if that lines up I propose a quick 30-min ops call this week to lock the exact node counts and timeline.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Director, Sales Engineering | Redwood Inference

Adding some technical sizing perspectives (quick notes):

- The 8x H100 baseline Kim suggested assumes 1) optimized batching for sessionized chat (we'll need request affinity hints) and 2) model variant quantized to int8 where we can (cost tradeoff).
- If the traffic has 30% embeddings, we can drop baseline nodes to 6x H100 and rely on cached embeddings for repeated vectors; embeddings-heavy profile favors GPUs with higher memory bandwidth vs raw TFLOPS.
- Burst policy: recommend time-windowed burst tokens with a soft-rate limiter to prevent SLO violations and automatic fallback to a smaller model variant when the host pool reaches 90% utilization.
- Sizing sensitivity: we modeled 3 scenarios in the attached cost matrix (steady/peak/shifted peak) — the cost delta between H100 and A100 baseline over 3 months is ~28%.

Operational constraints: Singapore availability of H100s is limited in the late-June to July window. If Aperture needs a strict 2027-07-15 start, we should consider either
  a) reserving node capacity now (reserved capacity contract), or
  b) starting with A100s for month 1 and migrating to H100s once available (requires migration plan but is feasible).

I'll also flag this with supply planning; attaching the brief cost matrix.

-Rishi
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
